talks.title: Crypto and Privacy Village: Day 2 Proceedings
talks.teaser: The full recorded proceedings and technical sessions from Day 2 of the DEF CON 29 Crypto and Privacy Village in Las Vegas.
talks.summary:
This recording captures the full proceedings of Day Two of the Crypto and Privacy Village at DEF CON 29, featuring presentations spanning modern cryptographic protocols, civil liberties, legal frameworks, multi-party computation, and secure messaging.

[00:03] The morning proceedings begin with technical discussions on classical cryptanalysis, block cipher design, and the long-term cryptographic resilience of AES-128 against algebraic and quantum attacks. At [03:18:00], attorney Anthony presents an analysis of digital privacy law and the Fourth Amendment, examining how third-party doctrines, government electronic surveillance, and the unregulated deployment of commercial facial recognition software impact civil liberties, disproportionately affecting communities of color.

[04:08:00] Matt Chung leads a technical session titled "Hacking on Multi-Party Computation," exploring the mathematics of threshold cryptography, homomorphic properties, and zero-knowledge proofs. Following Chung's talk, organizers of the "Through the Looking Glass" crypto challenge [04:42:00] walk through puzzle design, cryptographic riddles, and community solutions. The day concludes with "The Threat Hiding in Daylight" [05:38:00], an examination of end-to-end encryption protocols (Signal, KakaoTalk, WeChat, LINE), group chat key exchange mechanisms, and emerging privacy regulations in Taiwan and internationally.
